newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey unveils second ambitious revenue package.
newsitem.headline: Turkey unveils second ambitious revenue package.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan unveiled on Thursday his government's second revenue-raising package aiming to earn $10 billion.

The package aiming to mobilise 11 categories of resources included sale of state property, utilising unregistered precious metal stocks, a new witholding tax on state securities, and a reduction in taxes charged on domestic auto sales.

Erbakan, who was presenting the package at a joint press conference with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, said Turkey's troubled social security institutions would sell off their excess properties, including hotels, to finance their huge deficits.
Erbakan said the government expects 425 trillion lira income to be used by the institutions themselves, but did not give a time span.

He said a 10 percent witholding tax would be introduced on Treasury bills, bonds and revenue raising share certificates to be issued with 1997 maturity, but the tax would not apply to previously issued papers.

The government expects a 170 trillion lira revenue from the new tax next year. Income tax on interest earnings to be recorded from T-bills and bonds from 1997 was introduced earlier this year, but tax payments were to start in 1998.
